definition: A read-only package holding an application’s files and settings, used as the starting point for containers.
watch_for: A tag such as :release can be moved to a different image; a digest always means the same content.

definition: A running (or stopped) copy of an image, with its own isolated view of files, network, and processes.
watch_for: Removing a container deletes any files it changed, unless they were stored in a volume or mount.

definition: The main process inside a container. Docker sends it the stop signal, and the container ends when it ends.
watch_for: If a startup script launches the real server in the background and exits, the container stops too.

definition: A saved set of file changes. An image is a stack of layers, one for each build step that changes files.
watch_for: Deleting a file in a later step hides it but leaves it inside the earlier layer.

definition: The folder whose files a Docker build is allowed to copy, named by the last argument of docker build.
watch_for: COPY cannot reach files outside it, and anything inside it, including secrets, can be copied unless excluded by .dockerignore.

definition: Docker’s store of earlier build results, reused when a step and its input files have not changed.
watch_for: A cached step was not re-run, so it will not pick up changes from outside the build, such as a newer package online.

definition: A Dockerfile with more than one FROM, so tools used for building can be left out of the final image.
watch_for: The final stage still needs everything the application needs to run; copy it in deliberately.

definition: A fingerprint calculated from an image’s content, written like sha256:3f1a..., that changes whenever the content changes.
watch_for: One name can cover images for several processor types, and each of those has its own digest too.

definition: A server that stores images so other computers can push and pull them, such as Docker Hub.
watch_for: A successful push does not mean another machine has the network access or password needed to pull it.

definition: A folder from your computer made visible at a path inside a container.
watch_for: The folder keeps your computer’s owners and permissions, and it hides whatever the image had at that path.

definition: Storage managed by Docker or Kubernetes that lives separately from any one container.
watch_for: Surviving a container replacement is not the same as having a tested backup.

definition: A private virtual network that Docker creates so containers on it can reach each other by name.
watch_for: Being able to reach an address does not mean a name resolves, or that the app is listening on that port.

definition: A port on your computer that Docker forwards to a port inside a container, set with -p.
watch_for: The two port numbers can differ, and binding to 127.0.0.1 keeps the port private to your computer.

definition: One named part of a Docker Compose project, such as api or db, with its container settings.
watch_for: Starting services in order does not mean each one is ready; use health checks and have apps retry.

definition: A command run regularly inside a container to report whether it can do its job.
watch_for: It only tests what its command tests; a check that the process is up says nothing about its database.

definition: The part of Kubernetes that stores the cluster’s state, runs the API, decides where Pods run, and keeps everything in line.
watch_for: Existing containers can keep running while it is down, but nothing new can be changed or repaired.

definition: A controller’s loop of comparing what you asked for with what exists, and acting to close the gap.
watch_for: Submitting a change starts this process; it does not mean the change has finished.

definition: Kubernetes’ smallest unit of work: one or more containers that run together and share a network address.
watch_for: A replacement Pod is a new Pod with a new name and address; Services and controllers hide that from users.

definition: A Kubernetes object that keeps a set number of identical Pods running and rolls out updates to them.
watch_for: Its own labels and the labels on the Pods it creates are set in different places.

definition: The object a Deployment uses to keep an exact number of matching Pods running.
watch_for: Edit the Deployment, not its ReplicaSet; the Deployment will undo direct changes.

definition: A controller for Pods that need stable names and their own storage, such as databases.
watch_for: Stable names do not copy data between Pods or make a database highly available by themselves.

definition: A controller that runs one copy of a Pod on each suitable node, often for logging or networking agents.
watch_for: Nodes with taints the Pod does not tolerate are skipped.

definition: A controller that runs Pods until a task finishes successfully.
watch_for: Failed attempts are retried, so the task may run more than once; make it safe to repeat.

definition: A controller that creates Jobs on a schedule, like cron on Linux.
watch_for: A schedule does not guarantee the work happens exactly once per run.

definition: A named area inside a cluster for grouping objects and applying permissions and quotas.
watch_for: Namespaces do not block network traffic between Pods unless NetworkPolicies say so.

definition: A rule that picks objects by their labels, such as app=dispatch. Services and Deployments use them to find Pods.
watch_for: A selector can be perfectly valid and still match no Pods at all.

definition: A stable name and address in Kubernetes that forwards traffic to a changing set of matching Pods.
watch_for: Its name can resolve even when no ready Pods are behind it, so requests still fail.

definition: The list of Pod addresses a Service is currently sending traffic to, with whether each is ready.
watch_for: Check it when a Service exists but requests fail: an empty list means no Pods were selected or ready.

definition: A Service type that opens the same port on every node and forwards it to the Service’s Pods.
watch_for: The port is on the node machines, not automatically on your own computer.

definition: A set of HTTP routing rules, such as which hostname or path goes to which Service.
watch_for: It does nothing without an ingress controller running in the cluster to carry out the rules.

definition: A newer set of Kubernetes routing objects (GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute) that splits infrastructure from app routing.
watch_for: An accepted route still needs a real request to confirm it works.

definition: A Kubernetes object holding ordinary settings that Pods can read as files or environment variables.
watch_for: Environment variables are read only when a container starts; restart Pods after changing them.

definition: A Kubernetes object for sensitive values such as passwords, with separate access controls.
watch_for: Its values are base64 encoded, not encrypted; anyone allowed to read the Secret can decode them.

definition: An identity that a Pod uses when it talks to the Kubernetes API.
watch_for: Having an identity does not grant permissions; RBAC decides what it may do.

definition: Role-based access control: Roles list allowed actions, and RoleBindings give those roles to users or service accounts.
watch_for: A RoleBinding only grants access inside its own namespace; use a ClusterRoleBinding for the whole cluster.

definition: A Kubernetes rule that says which Pods may send traffic to which other Pods or addresses.
watch_for: It is only enforced if the cluster’s network plugin supports it; test allowed and blocked traffic.

definition: Pod or container settings that control its user, special permissions, and filesystem access.
watch_for: A read-only filesystem may still need a small writable folder, such as /tmp, for the app to work.

definition: A Linux feature that limits which low-level system operations a process may request.
watch_for: It narrows what a process can do but does not replace running as a non-root user.

definition: The amount of CPU and memory a container asks for; Kubernetes uses it to decide which node has room.
watch_for: A CPU request is not a cap; a container can use more CPU if it is free.

definition: The most CPU or memory a container is allowed to use.
watch_for: Going over a CPU limit slows the container down; going over a memory limit gets it killed.

definition: A check that decides whether a Pod should receive traffic right now.
watch_for: Failing it removes the Pod from the Service but does not restart it.

definition: A check that tells Kubernetes to restart a container if it keeps failing.
watch_for: If it depends on a database, a database outage restarts every Pod and makes things worse.

definition: A check that gives a slow-starting app time before liveness and readiness checks begin.
watch_for: Set its allowance to cover how long the app really takes to start.

definition: A PersistentVolumeClaim: a Pod’s request for storage of a certain size and type.
watch_for: A claim stuck in Pending may be waiting for a Pod to be scheduled, not missing storage.

definition: A PersistentVolume: a piece of storage in the cluster that can be bound to one claim.
watch_for: Its reclaim policy decides what happens to the data when the claim is deleted; Retain keeps it but is not a backup.

definition: A named kind of storage, with the settings used to create volumes for claims automatically.
watch_for: WaitForFirstConsumer waits to create storage until a Pod using it is scheduled, so it lands on the right node.

definition: The Container Storage Interface: the standard way storage plugins connect to Kubernetes.
watch_for: A manually created local volume does not exercise a storage plugin at all.

definition: The Container Network Interface: the standard way network plugins give Pods their network connections.
watch_for: A node showing Ready does not prove Pods on different nodes can reach each other or resolve names.

definition: The Container Runtime Interface: how the kubelet asks a runtime such as containerd to run containers.
watch_for: crictl talks to that interface directly; ctr is containerd’s own lower-level tool.

definition: The agent on each node that starts the Pods assigned to it and reports their status.
watch_for: Containers keep running if the kubelet stops, but nothing on that node is updated or reported.

definition: A tool that sets up a Kubernetes cluster’s control plane and joins nodes to it.
watch_for: It does not install a network plugin or a load balancer for you.

definition: A Pod the kubelet runs directly from a file on the node, used for control-plane parts such as the API server.
watch_for: Deleting it through kubectl does nothing lasting; change or remove the file on the node instead.

definition: The database where Kubernetes stores all of its objects.
watch_for: An etcd backup does not include the data inside your applications’ volumes.

definition: The majority of members a group needs to agree before it can make changes.
watch_for: Three etcd members can survive one failure; adding a fourth does not let it survive two.

definition: The file kubectl reads to know which clusters exist, how to log in, and which one to use.
watch_for: It can contain keys and tokens, so treat it like a password file.

definition: The encryption used by HTTPS, which also proves the server is who it claims to be using certificates.
watch_for: Turning off certificate checks hides the problem instead of fixing it.

definition: A small Kubernetes object that is renewed regularly, used for node heartbeats and choosing leaders.
watch_for: A recently renewed lease is better evidence a node is alive than an old Ready status.

definition: The HorizontalPodAutoscaler: it adds or removes Pods automatically based on measurements such as CPU use.
watch_for: It needs resource requests on the Pods and a working metrics server to measure against.

definition: A package manager for Kubernetes that turns templates, called charts, into objects and tracks installed releases.
watch_for: Check the rendered objects and the running Pods, not just that Helm reported success.

definition: A tool built into kubectl that builds Kubernetes files from a shared base plus small per-environment changes.
watch_for: A patch can apply cleanly and still change the wrong field; look at the output of kubectl kustomize.

definition: A controller that knows how to run a particular application, usually managed through its own custom object types.
watch_for: Adding a custom object type does nothing until a controller acts on it.

definition: A way of working where a controller keeps the cluster matching files stored in Git.
watch_for: A manual fix in the cluster gets undone unless you also change Git.

definition: A service level objective: a target for how reliable a service should be, such as 99% of requests succeeding over 30 days.
watch_for: It needs a clear definition of good requests, total requests, and the time window to be measurable.

definition: A software bill of materials: a list of the components inside an image.
watch_for: Knowing what is inside is not the same as knowing it is free of security problems.

definition: Replacing a password or key, updating everything that uses it, and making sure the old one no longer works.
watch_for: Changing a Secret does not mean running Pods are using the new value yet.

definition: Actually restoring a backup somewhere safe and checking the data and application work.
watch_for: A backup command finishing without errors does not prove the backup can be restored.
